# Cavco Takes Housing Affordability Message to Arizona Leaders at LACT 2026


Published On: August 21, 2026


•


2 min read


•


**Cavco at the 2026 League of Arizona Cities and Towns Conference**


Cavco Industries participated in the 2026 League of Arizona Cities and Towns Annual Conference, held August 18-21 at the Arizona Biltmore in Phoenix. The League’s signature event draws more than 1,700 Arizona mayors, councilmembers, and appointed officials together each year to address the challenges and priorities facing communities across the state.


Cavco attended with a display booth and a featured speaking role, with **President and CEO Bill Boor** joining a panel discussion titled *Housing Arizona: Attainable Solutions, Innovative Models & Community Trust* – making the case to Arizona’s municipal leaders that factory-built housing is a practical, scalable answer to the state’s growing affordability crisis.


Boor challenged the outdated zoning restrictions that continue to limit where manufactured homes can be placed.


> “We’re prohibited in various ways from putting our houses in a lot of cities and towns across the country,” he said. “I’ll argue that’s really old thinking about what our products are.”


He also pointed to demonstration projects as the most effective way to shift perceptions.


> “You’re looking for a city that says, ‘We’re not going to change everything, but we’ll take this one place and give this a shot so people can see what it looks like,” Boor said. “We can talk all day, but seeing is believing. Breaking down some of the mindsets takes examples.”


The conversations clearly resonated with attendees.


“The response from cities across Arizona was clear and consistent – every community confirmed a housing shortage in the affordable segment,” said **Tom Green, Cavco’s Director of Regional Sales** . “We left with site visits scheduled in multiple Arizona cities, a potential plan submission opportunity in another, and a developer partner as well. We came in hoping to identify cities willing to partner on manufactured housing solutions. We found them – and the work has already begun.”
